subject: Wrong edition of a textbook
situation: You bought a chemistry textbook at the campus bookstore last week. Today your professor told the class that you need the newest edition, but you have an older one. You still have the receipt.
bullets: Say why the book is a problem
Ask how you can exchange it

subject: Joining the swimming club
situation: You want to join the university swimming club, but you have not found any information about it on the website. You can swim, but you are not a very fast swimmer.
bullets: Ask a question about the schedule or the price

subject: Kitchen cleaning
situation: You and your roommate Alex share a small kitchen. Lately, dirty dishes have stayed in the sink for several days, and you want to solve the problem in a friendly way.
bullets: Suggest a simple plan for cleaning

subject: Absence next Tuesday
situation: You have a dentist appointment next Tuesday at the same time as your history class. The appointment was very hard to get, so you do not want to change it. Next week the class will have a short test.
bullets: Say what you can do to catch up

subject: Lost student card
situation: You think you left your student card on the campus bus this morning. The bus was number 4, and you got off near the science building at about 8:30. You need the card to enter the library.
bullets: Describe what you lost and where
Ask if anyone has found it

subject: English conversation club
situation: You saw a poster for an English conversation club at the Language Center. You would like to practice speaking with other students, but the poster does not say when the club meets.
bullets: Describe how well you speak English now

subject: No Wi-Fi in my room
situation: The Wi-Fi in your dormitory room stopped working three days ago. Other students on your floor have internet, and you need it to send your homework before the deadline on Friday.

subject: My birthday dinner
situation: Your birthday is next Saturday, and you are planning a dinner at a small restaurant near campus. You would like Emma, who is one of your best friends, to come.
bullets: Ask if she needs any special food

subject: Choosing a class
situation: You need to choose one more class for next semester. You are interested in both Introduction to Psychology and Basic Statistics, but you can only take one of them.

subject: Vegetarian meals
situation: You are a vegetarian and eat in the university dining hall every day. You have noticed that there is usually only one vegetarian dish, and it is often the same one.
bullets: Suggest one or two new dishes
Thank her for considering your idea

subject: Letter of recommendation
situation: You are applying for a summer exchange program, and the application requires a letter of recommendation from a professor. You took Professor Hall's course last year and received a high grade. The deadline is in three weeks.
bullets: Ask Professor Hall for a letter
Remind him why he knows your work well
Offer information that will make the task easier

subject: Missing scholarship document
situation: You received a message from the Financial Aid Office saying that a document is missing from your scholarship file. You submitted all the required papers last month and kept a copy of the confirmation. The scholarship payment is due soon.
bullets: Explain why you are surprised by the message
Describe what you did to submit your documents

subject: Request to change rooms
situation: Your dormitory room is next to a lounge where students often talk and play music until after midnight. You have asked them to be quiet several times, but nothing has changed, and you are having trouble studying for exams.

subject: Joining your research project
situation: Dr. Ibrahim gave a talk about her research on local bird populations. You found it fascinating and would like to get involved as a volunteer, although you have no laboratory experience.
bullets: Express your interest in the project

subject: A late-night study space
situation: The main library closes at 10 p.m., but many students study much later, especially before exams. Some of them have to go back to noisy dormitories or to expensive cafés, and you think the university should offer a better option.
bullets: Explain how it would benefit students

subject: Help with interview preparation
situation: You have been invited to a job interview at a local company for a summer position. This is your first formal interview, and you feel nervous. The Career Center offers practice sessions, but the schedule is full this week.
bullets: Say what kind of help you need

subject: Rescheduling our meeting
situation: Your group is preparing a presentation for next Monday. You planned to meet on Thursday, but your work shift has just been changed and you cannot come. Jordan is the group leader and has been organizing the project.
bullets: Propose a new time or another way to meet
Offer to complete some extra work

subject: Student open mic night
situation: There is a small café near campus where students often study. You belong to the university music club and think the café would be a good place for a monthly open mic night, when students could perform songs and read poems.
bullets: Explain why it would be good for the café

subject: Question about my quiz grade
situation: You received a grade of 6 out of 10 on a quiz, but you think one of your answers was correct. You have compared your answer with the textbook and with your lecture notes, and you believe the question was a little unclear.
bullets: Ask whether the grade could be reviewed

subject: Sending my transcript
situation: You need to send an official transcript to a university in another country. The application deadline is in ten days, and you have heard that the Registrar's Office sometimes takes a long time to process requests.
bullets: Ask about the fastest way to send it

subject: Extension for my report
situation: You were chosen to represent your university at a student conference next week. Because of the travel and meetings, you will not be able to finish the lab report for Dr. Levine's course by Friday, although you have already collected all the data.

subject: Construction noise near the lecture hall
situation: For the past two weeks, building work outside Lecture Hall B has been so loud that students cannot hear the professors. Several classes have been interrupted, and your class has an important lecture next Wednesday.
bullets: Explain how it affects your class

subject: Extended library hours during exams
situation: The university library currently closes at 10 p.m. even during final exams. Many students, including those who work during the day, find it difficult to study in their dormitories. You have spoken with classmates and believe that the dean could improve the situation at a reasonable cost.
bullets: Anticipate and answer a possible objection

subject: Alternative to the final paper
situation: Your course in design history requires a final paper of 3,000 words. You have been working on a related project, a small exhibition of student posters, and you believe it demonstrates the same learning outcomes more effectively than a traditional paper.
bullets: Show how the project meets the course goals
Propose a way to evaluate it fairly

subject: The new recycling policy
situation: The university has replaced all separate recycling bins with a single large container in each building. The office says this will increase participation, but you have noticed that people now throw almost everything into it, including food waste.
bullets: Explain why the policy may not achieve its goal

subject: Regarding the placement offer
situation: You were offered an internship at a large firm, but you have since been invited to join a research project in your department, which is more relevant to your future studies. You do not want to damage your relationship with the internship program.
bullets: Propose a way to stay in contact

subject: Correction request
situation: Last week the university newspaper published an article about student clubs. It stated that the Chess Club has only five members and meets irregularly. In fact, the club has more than forty members and meets twice a week. As the club's secretary, you want this corrected.
bullets: Explain why accuracy matters to the club

subject: Changes to my research method
situation: Dr. Kaplan approved your thesis proposal, which relied on a large survey. After starting the project, you found that few people respond to the survey, so you want to switch to a smaller number of in-depth interviews.

subject: Clarity of the room assignment process
situation: You and three friends applied together for a four-person apartment but were placed in separate buildings. The housing website says that group requests are given priority, yet no one has explained how the decision was made.
bullets: Request an explanation of the process
Propose a constructive way to resolve the situation

subject: Scheduling conflict with a guest seminar
situation: A well-known economist will give a guest seminar next Thursday, but it overlaps with Professor Brandt's tutorial. Attending the seminar would help your thesis, and the tutorial that day covers material you already know well.
bullets: Justify why attending the seminar is valuable
Offer a plan to make up the missed tutorial
